transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (CTO - Lumos), James O'Neill (Infra Lead), Priya Raman (ML Eng)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG quickstart and options between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is evaluating self-serve API for quick integration, curious about free credits, time-to-first-token, and security/compliance for pilot. Follow ups: pricing, SOC2/security docs, pilot scope and bench.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey folks thanks for joining, you all there?
[00:06] Sofia: yep, hi Maya, thanks, we're excited, i'm Sofia cto at lumos, James and Priya are with me.
[00:12] James: morning, yep, thanks.
[00:15] Maya: great, quick run through agenda: confirm their use cases, talk quickstart/free credits and time-to-first-token, map hosted vs dedicated vs private fit, security check, and proposed next steps. sound good?
[00:26] Sofia: sounds great.
[00:30] Ethan: hi everyone, ethan from redwood se, i'll jump in on latency and infra questions.
[00:35] Priya: cool, thanks.

[01:05] Maya: so can you walk us through the three main use cases you're thinking about so we can size things properly?
[01:12] Sofia: sure, we have chat-assist inside our product for customer support, a code-gen helper for internal tools, and an embeddings-based search for docs retrieval. priority is support chat first.
[01:23] Priya: the chat is latency sensitive, want sub-300ms p95 for short answers, but cost matters too, we're a startup.
[01:32] James: infra wise we use GCP, internal infra team manages VPCs and we have strict egress policies.

[01:50] Ethan: ok that helps. for quickstart, our hosted API gets folks from sign-up to first-token in minutes - we provide free credits for trials and a quickstart repo, usually time-to-first-token is under 15 minutes if you follow the SDK steps.
[02:08] Maya: yeah the PLG flow is intentionally smooth: self-serve API keys, quickstart samples, and pre-provisioned models in the catalog.
[02:16] Priya: great - how do the free credits work? limit per account or per project?
[02:22] Maya: typically we give a fixed trial credit bundle tied to the account, it's redeemable during onboarding, and we can top up for pilot partners. i'll include the exact redemption steps in the email.

[02:45] Sofia: ok on hosted, what are the main tradeoffs vs dedicated or private?
[02:52] Ethan: hosted is fastest to get started and lowest friction, but shared infra can mean tail latency variability and less control over data residency. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more consistent throughput/latency and better isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance - full network control, KMS integration and audit logs. dedicated and private have longer provisioning lead times.
[03:19] James: provisioning times - ballpark?
[03:22] Ethan: dedicated provisioning is usually days to a couple weeks depending on capacity and contract; private (on-prem or VPC private control plane) is weeks and needs security onboarding.

[03:40] Priya: for our pilot we want to start hosted if possible, but need to validate latency at scale and ensure logs aren't retained past 30 days.
[03:48] Maya: we have retention controls per account and can set shorter retention windows; for enterprise customers we offer options to not retain customer payloads.
[03:56] Sofia: what about SOC2 and SSO? we require SOC2 and SAML for SSO.
[04:02] Ethan: we are SOC2 compliant and we support SAML/SSO integrations for enterprise. i'll send the security deck and SOC2 report.
[04:10] James: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[04:13] Maya: yes for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS; for hosted we offer managed keys but can support bring-your-own-key for higher tiers.

[04:32] Priya: curious about quantization and lower cost options - can we run smaller quantized models to hit cost goals?
[04:38] Ethan: yes, our model catalog includes quantized variants and our runtime picks kernels and quantization profiles based on latency/cost tradeoffs. the optimize tooling suggests batching and reasonable quant profiles for your workload.

[05:05] Sofia: any gotchas with prefix caching and conversation state? we have long-running convos with context.
[05:12] Ethan: we do KV cache and prefix caching - sorry sometimes the transcript system writes KV cash - but that can reduce token cost for repeated prefixes. we can configure cache TTLs per route.

[05:32] Priya: ok on benchmarks, we want a simple perf bench: 1k prompts, avg len ~80 tokens, 50 RPS peak, measure p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. can Redwood run that?
[05:43] Ethan: yes we can run an internal bench on hosted and also give guidance for a pilot on your account. for dedicated/private we can replicate workloads but would need a bit more setup.

[06:00] Maya: question about SDKs - you mentioned time-to-first-token under 15 minutes, are there language SDKs?
[06:06] Priya: we primarily use Python/Go.
[06:09] Maya: yep we have official SDKs in Python, Node/TS, and a simple curl-based quickstart. community SDKs for Go exist; we're working on first-party Go.

[06:25] Sofia: security again, audit logs are essential for us. do you surface token-level usage and tracebacks?
[06:32] Ethan: console shows token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, traces, and we can export logs to your SIEM.

[06:45] James: networking: we have strict egress and need to use private peering. can hosted work with that?
[06:52] Ethan: hosted typically goes over public endpoints; for private peering we usually recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Redwood Private deployment.

[07:10] Priya: ok makes sense. what about support SLAs during a pilot?
[07:14] Maya: self-serve gets community support, plus email support for trial users; for pilots we can provide SE assistance and faster responses - we'll detail that in the email.

[07:30] Sofia: competitors question: we evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic, and Replicate for self-host; how is Redwood different?
[07:38] Maya: our angle is production-first inference tooling across hosted/dedicated/private with transparent perf profiles and dev experience - so you can start self-serve but have a path to dedicated or private without rewriting. also Optimize tooling and rollout policies are differentiators.

[07:55] Priya: any pricing notes for pilot? we have tight budget.
[08:00] Maya: we'll send a pilot pricing guide; free credits cover initial smoke tests and we can offer a limited-time pilot uplift for startups.

[08:14] James: ok, on data residency - we prefer data routed within GCP europe region. do you have region controls?
[08:20] Ethan: yes we have region routing policies and can pin requests to specific regions; hosted coverage varies by region, dedicated can be provisioned in desired region, private lets you entirely control placement.

[08:38] Sofia: are there any portability concerns if we build on your API and later move to self-hosted solution?
[08:44] Maya: our API is model-agnostic and we encourage using pinned model versions; migration to dedicated/private keeps the same API surface so app changes are minimal.

[09:02] Priya: ok great - hypothetical: if we hit production needs, what does a minimal dedicated contract look like?
[09:08] Maya: minimal reserved vGPU pool depends on throughput; typical entry is a small reserved cluster for predictable capacity. pricing and term length vary; we'll include a sample contract template.

[09:28] Sofia: about the quickstart, we want to try it now. can you walk us through sign-up and redemption?
[09:34] Maya: sure - sign up at the console, verify email, create an API key, follow quickstart repo, and redeem free credits in billing. i'll send a step-by-step. often teams can get first token within 10-15 minutes.

[09:52] Priya: do you require ip allowlist for api keys?
[09:55] Ethan: we support ip allowlist and we have route-level auth options; for more secure flows we recommend service accounts in private deployments.

[10:08] James: ok, sounds good. any developer experience traps? we are concerned about prompt latency and streaming support.
[10:14] Maya: we support streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. streaming helps reduce time-to-first-chunk for chat.

[10:30] Sofia: one last question on billing visibility - can we get token-level cost breakdown for routes?
[10:35] Ethan: yes, console exposes token breakdowns by route, model, and you can export granular usage to billing.

[11:00] Maya: great, recap: i'll send the quickstart, free credits steps, and pilot pricing. ethan will share SOC2 and security deck plus do a rough latency/cost estimate. lumos will send sample prompts and expected RPS. we'll plan a deeper technical demo the week of 9/14.
[11:20] Sofia: perfect thanks, looking forward.
[11:25] Priya: thanks all.
[11:30] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
